question: Should OpenClaw expose dynamic Discord presence updates to plugins, and if so should the contract be a narrow Discord-owned runtime/action API rather than a broad `api.runtime.channel.discord` namespace?
rationale: The source already has internal gateway presence machinery and a gated message action, but promoting that capability to third-party plugins changes a public API and credential-backed mutation boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve narrow Discord presence API
options.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off dynamic presence contract that wraps the existing gateway path with account routing, validation, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Use existing set-presence action only
options.body: Decline a new plugin-runtime API for now and document the existing gated `setPresence` message action as the supported dynamic path.

options.title: Fold into self-profile decision
options.body: Defer this narrower status/activity request to the broader Discord self-profile product/security discussion at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow Discord presence API
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off dynamic presence contract that wraps the existing gateway path with account routing, validation, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord auto-presence work and are the best available routing candidate for deciding how this should interact with existing presence behavior.
